problem: Unsupervised skill discovery learns task-irrelevant or hazardous behaviors due to uniform exploration, while existing guided methods need additional training and manual rules.
approach: COLLIE constructs a semantically coherent skill latent space from unsupervised data, enabling training-free guidance signals that work with sparse online human feedback.
contribution: COLLIE learns diverse, human-aligned skills while avoiding hazardous behaviors and achieving superior downstream performance with minimal human feedback.

problem: Standard dimension reduction fails to preserve global structure in single-cell transcriptomics because it doesn't adequately account for the geometric properties of biological data.
approach: InfoGlobe models RNA counts as Multinomial samples and leverages Fisher-Rao metric isometry between gene-level and gene-group statistical manifolds to preserve information geometry.
contribution: InfoGlobe preserves local-and-global cell-type geodesic distances, automatically discovers gene groups, and naturally mitigates batch effects without explicit alignment.

problem: Evaluating new models on existing benchmarks is expensive because generating and evaluating responses for all queries can be prohibitively costly.
approach: Leverages cached responses from previously-evaluated models using Data Kernel Perspective Space (DKPS) to predict benchmark performance and reduce query budget.
contribution: DKPS-based methods achieve the same accuracy as full evaluation with substantially decreased queries, and offline query selection improves prediction accuracy.

problem: Multimodal VAEs struggle with a trade-off between generative quality and coherence—generating realistic samples that are semantically consistent across modalities.
approach: Hölder++ implements true Hölder pooling without approximation, models distinct shared and private representations, and uses hierarchical inference for better disentanglement.
contribution: Hölder++ consistently improves the generative quality-coherence trade-off, yields more structured latent spaces, and learns shared representations useful for downstream tasks.

problem: Conventional architectures lose performance when input image color distribution changes at inference, and existing color equivariant methods introduce artifacts by approximating interval values as 1D translations.
approach: Builds color equivariant architecture by lifting saturation/luminance values from the interval to the circle (double-cover) to achieve true equivariance without approximation.
contribution: Resolves approximation artifacts, improves interpretability and generalizability, and achieves better performance on fine-grained classification and medical imaging than conventional and equivariant baselines.

problem: Generating executable CAD programs from images requires alignment between visual geometry and symbolic program syntax, but existing methods fail to scale with design complexity and rely on limited supervised data or expensive post-training.
approach: GIFT uses geometric feedback to bootstrap training data via Soft-Rejection Sampling (retaining diverse high-fidelity programs) and Failure-Driven Augmentation (converting near-misses into synthetic examples).
contribution: GIFT improves mean IoU by 12% over supervised baseline and reduces inference compute by 80% by amortizing test-time search into model parameters.

problem: Extending reinforcement learning gains to open-ended domains is difficult because ground-truth verification is unavailable, human annotation is expensive, and learned reward models are prone to reward hacking.
approach: RcRL exploits the generation-verification gap using pairwise preferences with a curriculum over rubric criteria, creating a more discriminative signal than absolute scoring.
contribution: RcRL preserves output entropy past 1000 steps (vs baselines plateauing within hundreds), achieves 70.5% preference on creative writing, and 25.4% improvement on HealthBench consensus.

problem: Jailbreak attacks bypass LLM safety alignment, but their mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering development of robust defenses.
approach: Identifies two functionally differentiated attention head types: Adversarially Compromised Heads (ACHs) in early layers that are suppressed by attacks, and Safety-Aligned Heads (SAHs) in mid-layers that maintain robust activations.
contribution: Shows ACH suppression drives jailbreaks while SAH activations persist, and reading these persistent activations yields competitive detection performance without training.

problem: Designing recommender systems faces the challenge of exploration-exploitation trade-off with incentive compatibility constraints in settings with stochastic user covariates.
approach: Two-stage algorithm integrates incentivized exploration with offline learning, using inverse proportional gap sampling (IPGS) in the second stage to maintain incentive compatibility.
contribution: Algorithm RCB achieves O(sqrt(KdT)) regret while satisfying incentive constraints, and discovers the trade-off between incentive budget and regret.

problem: Recovering radiometric fidelity from unknown dynamic range compression (like low-light enhancement and HDR reconstruction) is a blind inverse problem with unknown forward model and irreversible information loss.
approach: Introduces cascaded monotonic Bernstein (CaMB) operator to enforce monotonicity as hard architectural bias, integrated with diffusion models for geometric and semantic recovery.
contribution: CaMB-Diff significantly outperforms zero-shot baselines in signal fidelity and physical consistency on low-light enhancement, low-field MRI, and HDR reconstruction.

problem: Predicting structured scientific spectra requires capturing rich physical information while enforcing hard constraints like conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry, but existing methods treat them as unconstrained sequences.
approach: DeepSciReasoner combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning to capture spectral structure while respecting underlying physics.
contribution: Substantially improves prediction accuracy on eDOS, phDOS, XANES, and Raman spectra while maintaining physical consistency across all spectra types.

problem: Time series forecasting requires both semantic understanding of context and stochastic modeling of temporal dynamics, but existing approaches rely on either LLMs for semantics or diffusion models for generation, each inadequate alone.
approach: CoGenCast couples pre-trained LLMs with flow-matching by reconfiguring LLM attention for bidirectional encoding and integrating flow-matching for temporal evolution modeling.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on multiple benchmarks and naturally supports multimodal forecasting and cross-domain unified training.

problem: General continual learning systems must adapt to evolving environments with blurry task boundaries and online datastreams, but pretrained model-based methods struggle to reconcile diverse temporal information in a single pass.
approach: MePo uses meta-learning on pseudo task sequences from pretraining data and initializes meta covariance matrix as reference geometry for robust output alignment.
contribution: Achieves 15.10% improvement on CIFAR-100, 13.36% on ImageNet-R, and 12.56% on CUB-200 in rehearsal-free continual learning without needing task boundaries.

problem: Reinforcement learning fine-tuning of Vision-Language Models is prohibitively expensive, and existing methods port LLM techniques without exploiting VLMs' intrinsic text-vision alignment during reasoning.
approach: FOCUS-RL derives lightweight alignment metrics (PVA for sample difficulty, RVA for CoT quality) from dynamic text-vision alignment patterns to enable automated curriculum and dense supervision.
contribution: Achieves 2.5x–4x faster convergence over vanilla GRPO and +4.4 average accuracy gains across six benchmarks and multiple VLM families.

problem: Locally constrained decoding (LCD) for enforcing schema constraints on LLM outputs results in biased sampling because it myopically masks tokens without accounting for global dependencies.
approach: Proposes constructing globally constrained decoding (GCD) and probabilistic GCD (P-GCD) proposals for sequential Monte Carlo by tensorizing finite automata and circuit-multiplying them.
contribution: GCD and P-GCD converge faster to target distribution than LCD with fewer particles on function calling, keyword generation, and SQL generation tasks.

problem: Existing explicit surface reconstruction methods achieve strong performance but rely on test-time optimization, resulting in prohibitive runtimes of several minutes.
approach: FastSESR uses a lightweight triangular candidate network (TCN) with edge-factorized parameterization for efficient triangle extraction, followed by offset optimization network for refinement.
contribution: Accelerates surface reconstruction by at least 20x over prior methods while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality on scene-level datasets.

problem: Parallel decoding for diffusion LLMs is difficult because each denoising step provides only token-wise marginal distributions, while unmasking multiple tokens requires accounting for inter-token dependencies.
approach: DAPD uses self-attention to induce a conditional dependency graph and performs parallel decoding by selecting independent sets on the graph.
contribution: Improves accuracy–steps trade-off over existing methods and enables more globally distributed parallel updates exploiting any-order generation capability.

problem: Adversarial training fails in long-tailed settings due to severe robustness degradation on tail classes, caused by posterior mismatch where coarse-grained labels collapse class posteriors.
approach: PAT learns a posterior surrogate for fine-grained probabilistic supervision and integrates weight perturbations to encourage flatter loss landscapes.
contribution: Improves robustness with especially large gains on worst-class, and theory shows accurate posteriors tighten class-frequency estimation and robust generalization bounds.

problem: The Natarajan dimension characterizes learnability for finite label spaces, but fails for multiclass partial concept classes with unbounded label spaces.
approach: Shows Daniely-Shalev (DS) dimension characterizes learnability and reveals the Disambiguation Paradox: simple disambiguation schemes can destroy learnability while richer labeling preserves it.
contribution: Provides PAC learnability characterization for partial concept classes in multiclass settings and characterizes label-complexity vs sample-complexity trade-offs.

problem: Scaling inference-time compute in transformers trains them to emit explicit chain-of-thought tokens, but these cannot be applied during pretraining and rely solely on serial verbalization.
approach: Thoughtbubbles natively performs parallel adaptive computation in latent space by learning to fork or delete residual streams, forming 'bubbles' of computation mid-network.
contribution: Outperforms both standard decoder LMs and non-adaptive parallel methods on perplexity/zero-shot evals using half the training budget, achieving competitive GSM8K with half token budget.

problem: Vision-language pre-training for 3D CT imaging struggles with inefficient visual backbones and coarse semantic alignment between images and radiology reports.
approach: Proposes CNN-ViT hybrid encoder for efficient local detail capture, disease-level contrastive learning with learnable query tokens, and diagnosis-aware prompt strategy.
contribution: Achieves 84.4% AUC on CT-RATE (+5.1%), 75.4% on Rad-ChestCT (+5.4%), and +9.8% on 60-disease benchmark with strong transfer to report generation.

problem: Training generalist robot policies for diverse embodiments requires prohibitively costly data collection and retraining for each new embodiment.
approach: AugE-Toolkit provides a scalable robot augmentation pipeline that augments OXE dataset across 9 different embodiments, creating OXE-AugE with 4.4M trajectories.
contribution: Augmenting datasets improves performance on augmented robots, unseen robots, and original robots under distribution shift, with 24-45% success rate improvement on real manipulation tasks.

problem: Mean-field variational inference is scalable but its independence assumption severely limits inference when the posterior is inherently coupled across instances.
approach: Copula-SVI augments amortized marginals with explicit vine-copula posterior and refines samples with Stein updates, using vine decomposition for efficient learning.
contribution: Enables efficient higher-order instance-level dependence modeling with consistent improvements over structured VI baselines on constrained clustering and time series.

problem: Verification of model outputs relies on imperfect LLM judges and reward models, and ground truth labels are time-consuming and expensive to acquire.
approach: FUSE improves verification by ensembling verifiers without ground truth by controlling conditional dependencies using spectral algorithms.
contribution: Matches or improves semi-supervised alternatives without any labeled data across diverse generators, verifiers, and benchmarks including GPQA Diamond and IMO questions.

problem: Red-teaming Vision-Language Models for toxicity detection treats image generation as a black box, providing only terminal scores without understanding when and how toxic semantics emerge.
approach: STARE treats the denoising trajectory as exploitable attack surface using hierarchical RL with prompt editor and T2I fine-tuning via GRPO to align toxicity across phases.
contribution: Achieves 68% improvement in Attack Success Rate and reveals Optimization-Induced Phase Alignment: toxicity concentrates in early semantic phases and late refinement phases.

problem: Current spoken dialogue systems fail on under-represented dialects and accents due to misidentifying input language, and standard fine-tuning is expensive and prone to overfitting.
approach: CLD integrates convex optimization into dialogue pipelines using multi-GPU ADMM in JAX, providing global optimality guarantees and fast polynomial-time training.
contribution: Achieves 97-98% accuracy in low-resource regimes with certified margin stability and provable robustness to feature perturbations.

problem: Beyond conditional average treatment effects, treatments may impact entire outcome distributions in covariate-dependent ways, but existing methods don't capture such distributional effects.
approach: Proposes novel estimand for conditional distributional treatment effects with doubly robust estimator that is minimax optimal, and develops test for homogeneity with valid type 1 error.
contribution: First test with provably valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives for global homogeneity of conditional potential outcome distributions.

problem: RLVR methods typically center trajectory rewards using per-prompt empirical means, which can be noisy and unstable especially in low-generation regimes.
approach: Proposes shrinkage estimators combining per-prompt and cross-prompt means inspired by Stein's paradox to improve per-prompt mean estimation accuracy.
contribution: Shrinkage baselines provably yield lower-variance policy-gradient estimators across algorithms and require no additional hyperparameters or computation.

problem: Traditional whole slide image (WSI) analysis via multiple instance learning is computationally expensive due to exhaustive patch-level processing, severely limiting efficiency and scalability.
approach: PathCTM formulates inference as dynamic information pursuit transitioning from low to high magnification with attention-guided pruning and confidence-aware early stopping.
contribution: Reduces required patches by 95.95%, shortens inference time by 95.62%, and maintains AUC without degradation compared to standard MIL methods.

problem: Training reliable Process Reward Models (PRMs) for scientific reasoning requires expert-verified step-wise labels, which are prohibitively costly to obtain.
approach: DC-W2S stratifies weak supervision into reliability regimes by intersecting Self-Consensus and Neighborhood-Consensus metrics, using curriculum sampling and reliability-aware masking.
contribution: Enables training robust PRMs for complex reasoning without exhaustive expert annotation, proving strategic data curation more effective than indiscriminate training.

problem: Average run length (ARL) and average detection delay (ADD) are widely used optimality criteria for changepoint detection, but their application to real datasets with limited and irregular lengths is hindered.
approach: Proposes non-parametric KM-ARL and KM-ADD estimators by drawing analogy to survival analysis to model detection probabilities under sequence truncation.
contribution: Provides asymptotically unbiased estimators with provable bias bounds, enhancing robustness against limited/irregular sequences and improving model selection.

problem: Single-Positive Multi-Label Learning studies learning from incomplete supervision, but real-world annotations are biased toward salient categories, causing existing methods to miss less salient labels.
approach: PiSA constructs reliable class-wise prototypes from salient labels and leverages them to guide embedding learning for non-salient label recognition.
contribution: Theoretically shows SalSPML is harder than random SPML and demonstrates consistent improvements with average mAP gain of 3.16% on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Modern datasets contain samples of highly varying quality, and training directly on heterogeneous data yields suboptimal models for diffusion-based generation.
approach: Ambient Dataloops uses iterative dataset-model co-evolution where synthetically improved samples are treated as noisy at progressively lower noise levels, using Ambient Diffusion.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on unconditional and text-conditional image generation and de novo protein design with theoretical justification.

problem: Learning from language feedback in LLM agents lacks principled framing despite impressive empirical demonstrations, making it difficult to understand learning complexity.
approach: Formalizes LLF problem with sufficient assumptions for latency rewards, introduces transfer eluder dimension as complexity measure, develops no-regret algorithm HELiX.
contribution: Demonstrates cases where rich language feedback can be exponentially faster than reward learning, with performance guarantees scaling with transfer eluder dimension.

problem: Scaling RL with verifiable rewards is bottlenecked by limited existing verifiable data, where improvements saturate during training.
approach: Golden Goose synthesizes unlimited RLVR tasks from unverifiable text by constructing multiple-choice QA versions of fill-in-the-middle, generating diverse distractors.
contribution: Creates GooseReason-0.7M dataset with 0.7M tasks across math/programming/science, revives saturated models with sustained gains, and achieves SOTA on cybersecurity domain.

problem: Prompt injection attacks bypass LLM agents, but their mechanisms remain unclear, hindering defense development.
approach: Traces injection to role confusion where models perceive text source by how it sounds rather than labeled role, demonstrates via CoT Forgery attack.
contribution: Achieves 60% attack success against frontier models, shows degree of role confusion predicts attack success before generation, generalizes to standard agent injections.

problem: Current Video-LLM approaches for temporal grounding generate timestamps directly from unstructured visual tokens, leading to brittle numerics and inconsistent boundaries.
approach: F2G reformulates temporal grounding as verifiable Identify-then-Measure problem using predictive temporal perception and evidence-driven reasoning.
contribution: Consistently improves grounding accuracy across diverse benchmarks, transfers robustly across VLM backbones, and preserves general video understanding.

problem: Reconstructing temporal evolution from static sample snapshots is challenging for dynamic processes like cellular differentiation, requiring methods that scale in high dimensions.
approach: MMtSBM extends multi-marginal Schrödinger bridges to unpaired data via Iterative Markovian Fitting algorithm, enabling practical high-dimensional recovery.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on real datasets like transcriptomic trajectory inference in 100D, and for the first time recovers couplings/dynamics in very high-dimensional images.

problem: Low-count PET reconstruction is hindered by dissipative nature of prevailing generative models that wash out weak but diagnostically critical lesion signals.
approach: FlowPET reformulates reconstruction as volume-preserving transport via Separable Hamiltonian System with conjugate boundary conditions enforcing data consistency.
contribution: Surpasses state-of-the-art in SSIM/PSNR and more crucially exhibits superior recovery of low-contrast lesions in high-noise regimes.

problem: Language models show smooth scaling laws, but some capabilities exhibit sudden breakthroughs, with debate over whether these are emergent or metric artifacts.
approach: Shows breakthroughs are driven by continuous changes in probability distribution of training outcomes when performance is bimodally distributed across seeds.
contribution: Demonstrates sharp metric breakthroughs are produced by underlying continuous distribution changes, appearing well before most seeds achieve breakthrough.
